topStories.headline: Virginia State Police Investigate Fatal Officer-Involved Shooting at Staunton Walmart
topStories.dek: A man was shot and killed by a Staunton police officer Tuesday night at the Richmond Avenue Walmart; the officer has been placed on administrative leave while VSP leads the investigation.
topStories.body:
A Staunton police officer fatally shot a man at the Walmart located at 1028-C Richmond Avenue on the evening of Tuesday, September 22, at approximately 7:15 p.m. The man, identified by Staunton Police as Montique Treymayne Gaston, 39, of Portsmouth, was pronounced dead at the scene. The Staunton Police Department placed the officer involved on administrative leave, standard procedure for officer-involved shootings in Virginia.

At SPD's request, the Virginia State Police assumed control of the investigation. VSP asked the public to avoid the area while investigators processed the scene and worked to notify next of kin. Neither SPD nor VSP disclosed details about the circumstances that led to the shooting at the time of initial reporting.

Staunton Police said that once the VSP investigation concludes, a special prosecutor will review the case — also standard practice under Virginia law for officer-involved fatalities. Further information is expected to be released by state police at the conclusion of their investigation. Residents with questions may contact the Staunton Police Department or monitor updates from the Virginia State Police.

topStories.headline: Queen City Mischief & Magic Returns This Weekend, Closing Downtown to Traffic
topStories.dek: Staunton's beloved Harry Potter–inspired street festival, now in its 11th year, takes over the historic downtown September 26–27, with the city closing a portion of Beverley Street to vehicles starting Friday evening.
topStories.body:
Downtown Staunton transforms into an enchanted village this weekend as Queen City Mischief & Magic (QCMM) holds its 11th annual festival on Saturday and Sunday, September 26–27. The volunteer-run event draws more than 20,000 visitors to the city's historic streets, featuring costumed characters, themed dining and shopping, potion-making, wand dueling, and live performances. This year's edition adds programming from the worlds of Oz and Wicked alongside the longtime Harry Potter themes.

The City of Staunton announced that a portion of the downtown area will be closed to through traffic beginning at 5 p.m. Friday, September 25, and continuing through 5 p.m. Sunday, September 27. Festival-goers are encouraged to use the free shuttle running continuously on Saturday from the former Staunton Mall site to downtown between 8 a.m. and 10 p.m. Limited parking is available in the New Street and Johnson Street garages.

The Wildlife Center of Virginia will bring three animal ambassadors to the festival on Saturday, with live presentations scheduled for 12:30 p.m. and 2:30 p.m. The festival is free and open to the public; no tickets are required to attend, though some individual events at participating businesses may require advance registration. Full schedules and a festival map are available at queencitymagic.com.

topStories.headline: City Council Adopts Flood Resilience Plan, Unlocking State and Federal Grant Eligibility
topStories.dek: Staunton City Council unanimously approved the city's first Flood Resilience Plan on August 27, a five-year roadmap that now makes the city eligible for construction grants covering up to 95 percent of project costs.
topStories.body:
Staunton City Council voted unanimously on August 27, 2026 to adopt the city's first Flood Resilience Plan — a five-year, living planning document that lays out a long-term roadmap to protect neighborhoods, businesses, and infrastructure from severe weather and flooding events. With the plan now formally on the record, the city is eligible to apply for grants through Virginia's Community Flood Preparedness Fund (CFPF), administered by the Department of Conservation and Recreation.

The CFPF program has in prior years allowed project awards of up to $7.5 million. Because of Staunton's low-income designation, the city could qualify for up to 95 percent grant funding with a minimal local match for eligible capital improvement projects. The plan was prepared by Wetland Studies and Solutions, Inc. in partnership with engineering firm Wiley|Wilson, and was informed by public surveys and two community listening sessions held over the course of nearly a year.

Willow Hughes, the city's Environmental Programs Administrator, noted that the Wharf district — one of the neighborhoods covered in this paper — sits at the lowest point of a roughly 12-square-mile drainage area and is particularly vulnerable to rapid stream rises. The adopted plan is described as a living document that the city expects to revisit periodically. Residents may contact the Environmental Programs Division at StauntonStormwater@ci.staunton.va.us with questions.

moreNews.headline: Council Puts Data Center Rumors at Staunton Crossing to Rest
moreNews.body: In response to community concern, Mayor Michele Edwards issued a formal statement on behalf of Staunton City Council clarifying that no data center projects are planned, approved, or currently under review in the City of Staunton. The statement addressed public anxiety triggered by an April 2026 presentation that referenced a 2019 Staunton Crossing business plan which had listed data centers as a potential land use. City Economic Development Director Amanda DiMeo confirmed that data centers are not permitted under current city zoning, and that the 2019 reference was one option in an outdated document — not an active proposal. Council directed staff to proceed with an updated business plan for the city-owned Staunton Crossing site focused on advanced manufacturing and industrial uses.

moreNews.headline: Staunton Named Tree City USA for 30th Consecutive Year
moreNews.body: The City of Staunton has been designated a 2026 Tree City USA by the Arbor Day Foundation, marking the 30th consecutive year the city has received the recognition for its commitment to managing and expanding its urban tree canopy. The Tree City USA program recognizes communities that meet standards for a tree board or department, a tree care ordinance, a community forestry program, and an Arbor Day observance. The announcement appeared on the city's official newsroom at ci.staunton.va.us.
